column1: # Corrections to BirdNET+ Taxonomy's aliases for the labels of the shipped
# models. scripts/build_species_aliases.py merges these into the alias table,
# and an entry here wins over the taxonomy's own alias for the same label.
# Format: one entry per line, fields separated by a single tab. Lines starting
# with "#" and blank lines are ignored. Each entry has two or three fields:
#   superseded_name  the scientific name as a model's label spells it
#   canonical_name   the name to write the species under
#   ebird_code       optional, the taxonomy's eBird code for canonical_name.
#                    When present, the script stops with an error if the
#                    taxonomy no longer gives canonical_name this code, so a
#                    bridge cannot silently go stale. Vetoes leave it out.
# A label mapped onto itself vetoes a wrong taxonomy alias and keeps the
# The other entries bridge BirdNET v2.4 labels whose species the taxonomy
# moved to another genus without listing the old name as an alias. Without
# them, such a species is written under two names, the v2.4 one and the v3.0
# one, and its rows from the two models do not line up.
# Each bridge matches the v2.4 label's eBird code (eBird_taxonomy_codes_2024E.json
# from BirdNET-Analyzer) to the taxonomy's ebird_code, and is kept only where
# the species epithet survives the move, allowing for a changed gender ending.
# The script re-checks the code against the taxonomy on every run. The
# epithet check matters because after a split the code stays with one
# daughter species, and a code match alone would map the broader old species
# onto it. These v2.4 labels are splits and keep their own spelling:
# Pachycephala fulvotincta, Phaeomyias murina, Trachyphonus purpuratus and
# Bos frontalis is the gayal (mithun), a domesticated bovine of South and
# Southeast Asia that Perch has a label for. The taxonomy wrongly lists it as
# an alias of Stenella frontalis, the Atlantic Spotted Dolphin, so this entry
# Genus moves of BirdNET v2.4 labels.
